page: Amazon Web Services m1.small is a legacy, first-generation general-purpose instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with a single-core Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor running at 1.8 GHz on the i386 architecture. The instance includes 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.7 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 160 GB local hard disk drive (HDD). It features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps and does not include any graphics processing units (GPUs).

Benchmark results place the m1.small consistently in the bottom 10% of performance categories. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks both register at 969.19, reflecting the single-threaded nature of the hardware. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only small block cached memory at 66.65 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 6.94 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations are also constrained, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 344.87 and database operations scoring 456.15.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a low-resource, legacy tier. While it offers a low entry cost, its resource density and performance-per-resource ratios are low compared to modern instance families. It is not suitable for modern production environments, database hosting, or compute-intensive tasks. Appropriate workloads are limited to legacy application testing, basic utility scripting, or lightweight, non-critical background processes that do not require high network throughput or modern CPU instruction sets.
